drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna need the round-beam clause?
outcomeNote: The clause is justified by its concluding rule.

segments.he: עֲגוּלָּה רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִילּוּ הִיא מְרוּבַּעַת. הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? סֵיפָא אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּהֶיקֵּפוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים יֵשׁ בּוֹ רֹחַב טֶפַח.
segments.en: The mishna continues: If the cross beam is «round, one considers it as though it were square.» The Gemara asks: «Why do I need this» clause «as well?» Similar cases were already taught in the mishna. The Gemara answers: «It was necessary» to teach «the last clause» of this section, i.e., the principle that «any» circle «with a circumference of three handbreadths is a handbreadth in diameter.»
